title: Playwright bump to 1.63.0
summary: Main bumped @playwright/test 1.61.x -> 1.63.0 in all four repos, as the ONLY package.json change main made in this window in each repo. ins's package.json/package-lock.json conflict at merge is caused entirely by the branch's unrelated tooling divergence (Vite->webpack, joi, esbuild, dependency-cruiser etc.), not by the playwright line itself. animals, plants and tests all trial-merge package.json/package-lock.json with zero conflict markers, and for tests the four touched files (package.json, package-lock.json, Dockerfile, bin/update-visual-baselines-linux.sh) were never touched by the branch at all, so the merge takes main's copies verbatim. The branch itself never independently bumped playwright anywhere -- it is still pinned at 1.61.0 (1.61.1 in tests) on all four repos today.

animals: 8a3bc877 chore(deps): bump Playwright to latest (1.63.0) (#361) -- squashed PR merge that also folds in the pinned-npm lockfile regen follow-up
plants: ecccaad chore(deps): bump Playwright to latest (1.63.0)
7b121f9 fix: regenerate package-lock.json with pinned npm version

files.note: Branch's whole devDependency tree diverged (Vite removed, webpack/postcss/esbuild/husky/eslint-plugin-sonarjs added, joi promoted from implicit to explicit dep) so the same textual region as the @playwright/test line conflicts wholesale. Branch is still at 1.61.0 on this line; main's only edit is 1.61.0 -> 1.63.0.
Same root cause as package.json -- the lockfile trees diverged too far for a line merge to be trustworthy even where it would technically resolve.
git merge-tree auto-merges with no conflict message; branch's package.json context around the @playwright/test line is untouched, so main's 1.61.0->1.63.0 edit applies as a clean 3-way merge.
Auto-merges with no conflict. Recommend an `npm ci` verification pass after merge as a safety net even though no textual conflict exists, per the general lockfile-regeneration strategy.

Branch never touched this file since the merge base (confirmed by empty `git log -- package.json` over the branch range), so the merge is a straight fast-forward of main's content onto the branch's copy.
Base image bump mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v1.61.1-jammy -> v1.63.0-jammy, to keep the ZAP/Playwright container's browser binaries matched to the installed test runner version.
PLAYWRIGHT_IMAGE default bumped to match the Dockerfile.

branchEquivalent.evidence: Branch package.json still reads "@playwright/test": "1.61.0" in ins, animals and plants, and "1.61.1" (with "@playwright/cli": "0.1.14") in tests -- verified today by reading the blob directly from origin/feat/NO_JIRA-frontend-alignment in all four repos. The branch never touched these lines since the merge base.

verdictWhy: ins needs manual resolution (real conflict, caused by unrelated tooling divergence) plus a lockfile regeneration. animals, plants and tests auto-merge cleanly with no action required beyond an optional `npm ci` sanity check, but the cluster as a whole is not fully 'clean' because of ins.

resolutions.take: Take the branch's package.json as the base (it owns the whole dependency tree shape). Bump the single line "@playwright/test": "1.61.0" -> "1.63.0". Nothing else in main's package.json diff applies (main changed no other dependency).
resolutions.why: main's package.json diff for ins touches exactly one line; every other divergence in this file is the branch's own tooling convergence work, which the ledger already owns.

resolutions.take: Do not hand-merge. After resolving package.json, run `npm install` under the pinned npm 11.6.2 (package.json's own packageManager field, already present on the branch) to regenerate package-lock.json from scratch, then `npm ci` to prove it installs clean.
resolutions.why: The lockfile trees are too divergent for a trustworthy line merge; a full regen under the pinned npm version is the only way to guarantee `npm ci` passes in CI, matching how the branch's own earlier lockfile-regen commits (question 17) were done.

resolutions.take: Accept the clean git auto-merge as-is (proven identical to a hand-check: no conflict markers, main's only change was the version bump). Run `npm ci` post-merge as a sanity check, not because a conflict is expected.
resolutions.why: Zero-conflict trial merge already verified with `git merge-tree`; nothing to hand-resolve.
Same reasoning; plants and animals share the same dependency tree shape on this file.

resolutions.take: Accept main's content verbatim via the merge (branch never touched any of these four files, so there is nothing of the branch's to preserve here).
resolutions.why: Confirmed via `git log <mergeBase>..origin/feat/NO_JIRA-frontend-alignment -- <path>` returning no commits for any of the four files.

preAlign.what: Apply the identical one-line bump ("@playwright/test": "1.61.0" -> "1.63.0") directly on the branch now, ahead of the main merge, then regenerate package-lock.json under npm 11.6.2.
preAlign.why: Removes the playwright-specific decision from the noise of the much larger structural package.json conflict the merge will still have to resolve for other reasons (webpack/joi/etc.); the version to land on is settled and verified before the real merge starts.

preAlign.what: Apply the same one-line bump directly on the branch now and regenerate the lockfile under npm 11.6.2.
preAlign.why: Makes the eventual main-merge a true no-op for this file (nothing left for main to contribute), even though the merge already auto-resolves cleanly today.

preAlign.what: Apply main's four-file change set (package.json's two playwright lines, package-lock.json regen with plain npm, Dockerfile base image, bin/update-visual-baselines-linux.sh default) directly on the branch now.
preAlign.why: The branch has never touched these files, so pre-aligning is a straight copy of main's already-CI-proven change -- there is no branch content to reconcile.

behaviourChanges: Playwright test runner and bundled browsers move from the 1.61.x line to 1.63.0 across all four repos.

tests repo additionally bumps @playwright/cli 0.1.14 -> 0.1.21 and the ZAP/Playwright Docker base image + local baseline-update script default from v1.61.1-jammy to v1.63.0-jammy, keeping the CLI, the test runner and the browser image in step.
knockOn: A newer Playwright/browser build can shift visual baselines or timing-sensitive assertions; a full E2E run (including a `bin/update-visual-baselines-linux.sh` check in the tests repo) after the merge is the way to catch that, not an assumption that the bump is behaviourally inert.
ins's own Dockerfile does not reference a Playwright image tag (its E2E runs out of the tests repo, not its own image), so no second bump is needed there.

openQuestions.question: Should the pre-align commits (one per repo) be raised as their own visible commits ahead of the main-merge commit, or folded silently into the merge resolution?
openQuestions.default: Raise them as their own small commits ("chore(deps): bump Playwright to 1.63.0, pre-aligning with main") -- cheap, and it means the subsequent main-merge diff for this file is empty or near-empty, which is easier to review than a merge commit that silently changes a dependency version.
